slot.brief: List four ordering statements about first ionisation enthalpies across a period or down a group (including a Be/B or N/O type anomaly) and ask which statement is wrong.

stem: Which of the following orders of first ionisation enthalpy is incorrect?

verdicts.working: First ionisation enthalpies: Li ≈ 520, B ≈ 801, Be ≈ 900, C ≈ 1086 kJ mol⁻¹. Thus the correct order is Li < B < Be < C, so (A) is incorrect. The other listed orders are increasing.

working:
$I_1(\text{Li})=520 < I_1(\text{B})=801 < I_1(\text{Be})=900 < I_1(\text{C})=1086\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Thus option A reverses the order of B and Be.
$\text{C}<\text{O}<\text{N}<\text{F}$; $\text{K}<\text{Ca}<\text{Sc}<\text{Ti}$; $\text{Kr}<\text{Ar}<\text{Ne}<\text{He}$ are increasing orders.

Independent check: First ionisation enthalpies: Li ≈ 520, B ≈ 801, Be ≈ 900, C ≈ 1086 kJ mol⁻¹. Thus the correct order is Li < B < Be < C, so (A) is incorrect. The other listed orders are increasing.
solution:
Across a period, first ionisation enthalpy generally increases, but boron has a lower value than beryllium due to its higher-energy $2p$ electron.
$$I_1(\text{Li}) < I_1(\text{B}) < I_1(\text{Be}) < I_1(\text{C})$$
Hence the order in (D) is incorrect.
